newsitem.title: GERMANY: ALPINE SKIING-WACHTER JUST AHEAD OF ITALIAN RIVAL.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WACHTER JUST AHEAD OF ITALIAN RIVAL.

text.p: Italy's world champion Deborah Compagnoni and Austrian veteran Anita Wachter were embroiled in their second tense giant slalom battle in consecutive days in the Alpine skiing World Cup on Saturday.
Olympic champion Compagnoni, who won Friday's race on the German course just ahead of Wachter, had to settle for second place behind the Austrian in Saturday's first run.
But the times on the icy course were very tight ahead of the decisive second run at 1230 GMT.

Wachter clocked one minute 4.35 seconds, just 0.04 of a second faster than Compagnoni. Germany's Katja Seizinger, last year's overall World Cup champion who fell in Friday's race, was third, 0.07 behind Wachter.
"The lead is a bit of a surprise since I made a few mistakes," Wachter said.
Seizinger added: "The second leg is going to be tight."
